messages:
Maya: quick thread — ran quantization matrix for two candidate models and a short cost+quality scorecard for GTN. TL;DR recommendations at the bottom.

EvalBot: results uploaded from the run: model variants tested = [LlamaX-13B_fp16, LlamaX-13B_q4_0, LlamaX-13B_q4_1, Orca-7B_fp16, Orca-7B_q4_0]. Benchmark suites: convQA, summary-eval, hallucination-check, safety-check.

EvalBot: raw numbers (median across 10 seeds):
```
model,latency_ms/prompt,throughput_tok/s,cost_per_1M_tokens_usd,convQA_acc,summary_ROUGE-L,hallucination_rate
LlamaX-13B_fp16,310,120,35.4,0.84,0.62,0.07
LlamaX-13B_q4_1,240,160,12.8,0.82,0.60,0.09
LlamaX-13B_q4_0,230,170,10.7,0.79,0.58,0.11
Orca-7B_fp16,160,260,18.5,0.76,0.55,0.12
Orca-7B_q4_0,130,320,6.9,0.72,0.51,0.16
```

Sam: good, can you remind me what our target SLOs for GTN are? latency < 350ms p50 and convQA_acc >= 0.8 for the search assistant intent, right?

Maya: correct. For the search assistant we need >=0.8 convQA and p50 latency <350ms. For the writing assistant product we prioritize ROUGE-L and lower hallucination.

Jonah: reading the table -> LlamaX-13B_q4_1 looks like a nice sweet spot: convQA 0.82 (meets SLO), cost 12.8usd/1M tokens, latency 240ms. Orca-7B_fp16 is faster and cheaper than LlamaX_fp16 but quality is lower.

Kevin: two operational notes: 1) q4_1 is stable on our A100-ish fleet but q4_0 had occasional decode artifacts leading to that +0.02 hit in convQA. 2) KV cache savings: q4 variants reduce memory pressure which gives us ~20% higher concurrency in Dedicated.

Liz: product asks — what's your single recommended default for GTN (search assistant) vs fallback for high-accuracy tasks? Also any rollout caveats?

Maya: recommendation: 
- Default (GTN, search assistant): LlamaX-13B_q4_1 — meets convQA >=0.8, latency well under SLO, ~3x cheaper than fp16.
- Fallback (writing, long-form/high-quality): LlamaX-13B_fp16 for tasks where hallucination tolerances are low (ROUGE and hallucination gains).
- Budget mode: Orca-7B_q4_0 for microservices where hallucination risk acceptable and ultra-low cost is primary.

Maya: rollout plan: canary 5% traffic on Hosted for 48h with prompt-quality checks + evals every 2k requests. Monitor convQA and hallucination delta; auto-roll back if convQA drops >0.03 or hallucination increases >0.04.

Sam: what's the unit economics for the default vs fallback? need this for GTN pricing sheet.

EvalBot: unit econ snapshot (tokens per USD approximations):
```
model,cost_per_1M_tokens_usd,tokens_per_usd
LlamaX-13B_fp16,35.4,28265
LlamaX-13B_q4_1,12.8,78125
Orca-7B_q4_0,6.9,144928
```

Maya: so LlamaX-13B_q4_1 gives ~2.8x token throughput per dollar vs fp16. For typical GTN prompt sizes (prompt+response ~750 tokens) that maps to ~58k prompts per USD vs ~20k for fp16.

Jonah: recommended GTN product guidance for docs: default = q4_1 (latency/quality tradeoff), offer a toggled "high-quality" flag to route to fp16 for paid tiers. Keep budget tier on Orca-7B_q4_0.

Kevin: perf ops checklist: ensure quantized model uses our fp32 fallback path when decode anomalies detected; add metric alert on avg beam-breakdown rate. Also include a short re-eval job in the deploy pipeline that runs the 200-case hallucination-check.

Liz: thanks — please add a one-pager for GTN PMs with the decision matrix (cost vs quality) and the canary thresholds. Can you attach that to the PR?

Maya: will do. I'll open a tiny PR with the one-pager + the canary workflow and link the eval run artifacts. ETA this afternoon. :+1:

Sam: one more Q: do we need to lock quant config per customer on Dedicated? some customers care about exact fp16 behavior.

Maya: yes — Dedicated/Private customers should be able to pin fp16 vs q4 variants. We'll expose a rollout flag in the deployment spec.

EvalBot: note: follow-up experiment suggestion — try q5_0 on LlamaX-13B for heavy-cache workloads; early sims show potential cost parity with Orca-7B_q4_0 while keeping convQA closer to 0.8.

Jonah: nice. let's add q5_0 to next week's bench.

Kevin: I'll add the alert rules and the re-eval job to the deploy pipeline.

Maya: closing the thread — will post PR link here when ready.
